target: temporary workers.dev Worker and temporary Cloudflare R2 bucket

methodology.execution: Disposable Azure Node 22 clients used the production ThimbleDB browser read planner over HTTPS. TDB1 object reads, decryption, decompression, caching, index planning, and result validation used the current package code. Writes executed inside the temporary Cloudflare Worker against R2.

layouts.snapshot: Current encrypted immutable snapshot plus two declared secondary indexes.
layouts.trie: Current encrypted two-level content-addressed trie plus two declared secondary indexes.
layouts.bundle: Current bounded authority-side point-read bundle, limited to four objects and 4 MiB decoded.

indexes.equality: category equality with title and lastModified covering fields
indexes.range: lastModified range with title and category covering fields

methodology.primaryLatency: clientElapsedMs measured by the regional Azure caller around the complete operation
methodology.writeTimer: workerIoTimerMs is retained only as a secondary I/O-oriented timer

limitations: Azure regions approximate client geography and do not represent residential last-mile networks.
The temporary benchmark omitted OIDC login and production application rendering.
Node 22 executed the browser client code, so IndexedDB and browser scheduling were not measured.
One Cloudflare account and one R2 bucket placement were used.
Absolute latency varies with routing, platform load, and time of day.
The synthetic workload does not establish superiority over another database.
